Other predicates retain the same rounded form while attaching different claims to it. Qianyan Yuanzhang pairs “perfectly round” with “shining and flashing,” then says “large within large, narrow within narrow.” Hongzhi Zhengjue says that the form is neither the least bit deficient nor the least bit excessive. Chunan Furong Baining Yi also criticizes a fixed reading: he says later people take “the perfectly round and shining one” as the ultimate rule, yet do not know that the Way has no fixed body and that heading toward it goes astray. His warning prevents the dictionary from converting a recurrent description into one universal abstract definition. The adverbial form occurs 15 times in 11 texts, and the exact round-and-shining pairing occurs three times in three texts.
The sources predicate round completeness of experience or functioning, not a literal circular object.
